results.reason: Every condition was tested against the source texts (r21/pdf/P-1403.txt, P-1421.txt, and P-1421 Fig. 1 rendered from the PDF), and none fails for the A+T+ contrast. (1) Figures match the sources exactly: P-1403 p.5/7 A+T+ 7.81 (3.92-15.59), A-T+ 4.25 (1.60-11.31), A+T- 1.14 (0.58-2.24); P-1421 Table 2 p.4 NC to MCI p-tau217 high vs low 1.07 (0.73, 1.56) basic, 1.19 (0.75, 1.88) fully adjusted. The adjustment sets match (P-1403 p.4: age at classification, sex, education; P-1421 basic: age time scale, sex, education). (2) The closest thing to a matched figure is P-1421's continuous spline for p-tau217 NC to MCI (Fig. 1, p.3; basic model, reference = median). I read it from the rendered figure: about 1.18 (0.79-1.79) at z = 1 and about 1.36 (0.74-2.48) at the high end of the plotted range (z around 1.93). Even at that end the upper bound (about 2.5) stays below P-1403's A+T+ lower bound of 3.92. So P-1421 excludes a hazard of 4 or more even at extreme p-tau217 levels, and the gap is not an artefact of its 37%-high dichotomy. (3) The difference goes beyond uncertainty: 3.92 > 1.56, 1.88 and about 2.48, so the intervals do not overlap. It is not significance-only. (4) Condition 1 holds. The contrast is joint A/T rather than single-marker, but P-1403 shows the A+T+ effect runs through tau: amyloid alone is null in both papers (1.14 and 0.98), and P-1403 says 'almost all T+ participants were also A+' and that adding Abeta 'did not improve the prediction'. The reference choice barely matters: A-T- progressed 25/127 (19.7%) and A+T- 14/60 (23.3%). Family-history enrichment, assay, threshold, MCI definition and horizon are allowed differences under the brief. (5) Not a performance comparison. This concession weakens the pair: the A-T+ arm does NOT robustly meet condition 4. Its 1.60-11.31 excludes only the basic dichotomy, by 0.04. It overlaps the fully adjusted 0.75-1.88 and the spline's upper range (1.79 at z = 1; about 2.48 at z around 1.93). The pair qualifies on the A+T+ contrast alone, and the record should describe the A-T+ arm as within uncertainty. None of the candidate explanations is shown by either paper to be sufficient.

figures.P-1403: Cox HR vs A-T- (adjusted for age at classification, sex, education): A+T+ 7.81 (3.92-15.59), 16/21 progressed; A-T+ 4.25 (1.60-11.31), 5/7; A+T- 1.14 (0.58-2.24), 14/60; reference A-T- 25/127. T+ = plasma p-tau217 > 3.98 pg/mL (28/215 = 13%). Tau cut-off specificity 97%, sensitivity 34% for incident MCI (p.8).
figures.P-1421: Multistate Markov HR, NC to MCI, serum p-tau217 high vs low (cut 0.134 pg/mL; 803/2148 = 37% high): basic 1.07 (0.73-1.56), fully adjusted 1.19 (0.75-1.88). Continuous spline (Fig. 1, basic model, reference = median z-score), read from the rendered figure on a log axis at 87.9 px per ln unit: z = 1 about 1.18 (0.79-1.79); z around 1.93 about 1.36 (0.74-2.48). Abeta42/40 low vs high 0.98 (0.72-1.34). Counts of elevated p-tau217/NfL/GFAP: all null for NC to MCI (largest upper bound 2.17).
figures.comparison: A+T+ lower bound 3.92 exceeds P-1421's basic upper bound 1.56, its fully adjusted 1.88 and its extreme-level spline upper bound of about 2.48: no overlap under any P-1421 figure, so this arm qualifies. A-T+ lower bound 1.60 exceeds only the basic dichotomy (by 0.04). It lies inside the fully adjusted interval and the spline's upper range, so this arm is within uncertainty. Amyloid alone agrees (both null).

candidate_explanations: Population: first-degree family-history research cohort, mean age 65 at classification, against a random community sample aged 60+ (865 of 2148 aged 78 or over). P-1403 p.3: 'a longitudinal observational study of individuals with a first-degree family history of AD'.

Exposure contrast and threshold: joint A/T group against the double-negative reference, with T+ set 2 SD above Abeta-PET-negative CU adults (13% T+, 97% specific, 34% sensitive), against a single-marker split at a cut-off tuned for 10-year all-cause dementia (37% high). P-1403 p.10: 'The thresholds were selected to optimize the detection of AD pathology, not to detect MCI with no AD pathology.'

Age and comorbidity confounding of P-1421's dichotomy: the median p-tau217 is 0.07 pg/mL under 78 and 0.17 pg/mL at 78 or over, against a cut of 0.134 (Table 1, p.2), so 'high' largely tracks the oldest stratum, where chronic kidney disease is 62.5%. P-1421 p.5: 'AD blood biomarker levels increase with age, even in cognitively unimpaired individuals, suggests the potential need for age-adjusted cutoffs.'

MCI definition: consensus MCI requiring more than 1.0 SD impairment plus a subjective complaint and/or observed decline, against psychometric MCI (1.5 SD or more below the age-specific mean in one domain) with reversion to NC modelled. P-1403 p.4: 'participants needed to have a subjective memory complaint and/or have an objective decline witnessed over multiple cognitive follow-ups.'

Model: multistate Markov model on an age time scale, with death absorbing and unobserved NC to dementia forced through MCI, against a Cox model on time since plasma sampling. P-1421 p.7: 'individuals who progressed directly from normal cognition to dementia were assumed to have passed through a MCI phase'.

Matrix and assay: plasma on an in-house Gothenburg Simoa (Abeta by IP-MS) against serum on the ALZpath Simoa. P-1421 p.6: 'our results based on cut-offs derived within the SNAC-K cohort, may not fully extend to more diverse populations or alternative laboratory platforms.'

Selection in P-1421: 833 dementia-free participants lacked biomarkers and were older and sicker. P-1421 p.6: 'Since these individuals were at higher risk of dementia, their exclusion may have led to an underestimation of the results.'

Small exposure groups and horizon in P-1403: 21 A+T+ and 7 A-T+ over a mean 5.65 years after plasma, against 803/1345 over a mean 9.6 years. P-1403 p.10: 'Given this limitation and the fact that 20% of our reference group developed MCI, the HRs between groups should be interpreted with caution.'

checks.matched_figure: No same-contrast figure exists. P-1421 has no A/T classification and no AD-anchored threshold, and its under-78 and baseline-MCI-excluded analyses are only in the supplement. P-1403 prints no whole-sample single-marker HR. P-1421's continuous spline at the high end (about 1.36, 0.74-2.48) is the closest proxy. It reconciles the A-T+ arm, not the A+T+ arm.
checks.arithmetic: Log-axis calibration from gridlines: 1.0 at y = 413 px and 10.0 at y = 210.5 px, so 202.5/ln(10) = 87.9 px per ln unit. At x = 1335 (z about 1.93) the band runs from y = 333 to 439 with the line at 386: upper exp(80/87.9) = 2.48, lower exp(-26/87.9) = 0.74, point exp(27/87.9) = 1.36. At x = 1060 (z about 0.99) the band runs from 362 to 434 with the line at 398.5: 1.79 / 0.79 / 1.18.
checks.note_for_record: Report the pair on the A+T+ contrast. The A-T+ arm should be described as overlapping P-1421's fully adjusted and continuous estimates.

quotes.quote: Cox proportional hazard models showed a higher risk of progression from CU to MCI among the A+T+plasma and A−T+plasma (hazard ratio [HR] = 7.81, P < 0.001, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 3.92 to 15.59; HR = 4.25; P = 0.004, 95% CI = 1.60 to 11.31
Interestingly, amyloid markers did not improve the predictivity of the tau markers, which can be explained by the fact that almost all T+ participants were also A+.

Seventy-six percent (16/21) of the A+T+plasma group developed MCI compared to 23% (14/60) in the A+T−plasma group, 71% (5/7) in the A−T+plasma group, and 21% (25/127) in the A−T−plasma group (Figure 1A).

quotes.quote: Hazard Ratios (HR) with 95% Confidence Intervals (CI) are derived from multistate Markov models, using age as time scale and adjusted for sex and education. AD blood biomarkers were converted into z-scores and modeled using restricted cubic splines with 3 prespecified knots at 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles. The median value was chosen as reference for all the z-scored biomarkers.

quotes.quote: Notably, no association emerged between any of the examined biomarkers and the development of MCI among cognitively unimpaired participants.
